Intrinsic

in-TRIN-zik -- stress on the second syllable, TRIN. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Intrinsic is being essential to a thing's very nature; belonging to it from within.

Curiosity seems intrinsic to cats; no one has to teach a kitten to investigate an open box.

Worked Example

Two students read the same novel: one for the pizza party promised to the class, the other because she simply loves losing herself in a story.

The second student's motivation is intrinsic -- it comes from within the activity itself, not from an outside reward. Intrinsic describes whatever belongs to a thing's own essential nature.

How Intrinsic Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

inherent

inherent: existing as a natural, built-in part

essential

essential: absolutely fundamental to what a thing is

inborn

inborn: present from birth; natural

Antonyms

extrinsic

extrinsic: coming from outside a thing, not part of its nature

acquired

acquired: gained from outside over time

How Strong Is It? — inherent → intrinsic → essential

inherent vs. intrinsic

inherent vs. intrinsic: Inherent is the close, slightly milder cousin -- an inherent trait is naturally part of something, while calling it intrinsic insists it belongs to the thing's very core and would be there no matter what surrounds it.

essential vs. intrinsic

essential vs. intrinsic: Essential raises the stakes past intrinsic: an intrinsic quality belongs to a thing's nature, while an essential one is so fundamental that without it the thing would stop being itself at all.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of intrinsic.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — intrinsecus

Root — intrinsecus: inward, on the inside (Latin, from intra 'within' + secus 'alongside, following')

Put it together

Put it together: Here is an honest warning: intrinsic does not split into English building blocks the way this unit's other words do. Latin intrinsecus ('inward, on the inside') was borrowed into English as one fossilized piece — there was never a real English base word that had -ic added to it, much as 'public' and 'magic' only look like they end in the suffix. The meaning still fits beautifully — what is intrinsic lies on the inside, in a thing's very nature — but treat the -ic ending here as a look-alike, not a true building block.

Use the root in a new word: intramural

Use the root in a new word: intramural: The intra at the front of intrinsic is Latin for 'within' -- the same piece that starts intramural. Intramural sports are literally games played 'within the walls' (intra + muralis, 'wall') of a single school, just as an intrinsic quality lies within the thing itself.

Root Check

Word Choice

Intrinsic usually takes 'to' -- flexibility is intrinsic to gymnastics -- and pairs with value, worth, and motivation. Its perfect opposite is extrinsic: intrinsic motivation comes from loving the activity itself, extrinsic motivation from rewards stacked on top of it.
